A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same feature-absorption study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and the original experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gemma-2-2B classification, latent-ablation and absorption results, plus appendix spelling, editing and activation-patching experiments.

after.justification: V5 retains those empirical results and adds synthetic SAE experiments, evaluations on Qwen2 and Llama SAEs, and an ablation-metric comparison.

M1.justification: The main k-sparse-probing and integrated-gradients absorption detector remains unchanged. Appendix A.13 newly specifies projection-based detection variants accommodating multiple absorbing latents and weakly active main latents. These are proposed procedural extensions, explicitly unused in the main experiments.

E1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.3 add synthetic feature-recovery tasks with known underlying features, covering independent and hierarchical activation patterns, variable magnitudes and imperfect co-occurrence. This substantially expands the represented input conditions. The original English-token first-letter and full-spelling tasks remain.

E2.justification: LR probes remain the classification baseline, and the encoder-cosine versus k=1 sparse-probing comparison is retained (v1 A.3; v5 A.7). L1, TopK and BatchTopK are additional SAE systems being diagnosed; no competing absorption-detection baseline is added.

E3.justification: V5 introduces controlled four-feature and twelve-feature synthetic evaluation designs and evaluates additional L1/TopK SAEs on Qwen2-0.5B and Llama-3.2-1B. Appendix A.10 compares mean- and max-incorrect-logit ablation metrics on Gemma layers 0–3. The original 80/20 split and main detector thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New controlled analyses test whether absorption depends on hierarchical co-occurrence, fixed feature magnitudes, perfect hierarchy or an explicit L1 penalty (Section 3; Appendix A.3). Appendix A.10 adds empirical sensitivity analysis for the ablation metric. Earlier projection-removal, editing and activation-patching analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v5 introduces no uncertainty-estimation procedure. The new toy-feature magnitude variance describes input variability, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: V5 adds absorption findings for Qwen2/Llama SAEs (Figure 9c), synthetic full and partial absorption results (Figures 2 and 10–12; Tables 2–3), and higher absorption estimates under the max-logit metric (Figure 21). The original Gemma plots and case-study values, including F1 0.81 and decoder cosines 0.52/0.12, are retained.

T1.justification: V1 offers a heuristic sparsity argument. V5 Appendix A.2 adds explicit assumptions, a delta-parameterized encoder/decoder family, and proofs of perfect reconstruction and decreasing expected sparsity loss, Lsp = p11(2 − delta) + p10. These results are conditional on the specified orthogonal-feature, hierarchical, bias-free ReLU setup.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion move from identifying classification failures and suspecting a sparsity mechanism to claiming that hierarchical features cause absorption even when features are linear and sparse. V5 also broadens the empirical claim beyond Gemma/JumpReLU to every tested SAE across several models and architectures.

C2.justification: V5 explains partial absorption through weak parent-latent corrections and explains why absorption can benefit TopK reconstruction without L1 loss. It adds tradeoffs between causal verification, layer coverage and detecting partial or multiple-latent absorption. Limitations shift from one model/architecture to limited non-JumpReLU coverage; v1’s explicit ground-truth-label limitation is omitted.

D1.justification: V5 adds synthetic-data generation details, toy training coefficients and budgets, and SAELens training information including 500M tokens and a 40GB A100 (Appendix A.9). It omits v1’s experiment-repository link. Some new details remain inconsistent: Appendix A.3 states BatchTopK k=2, while Figure 12 says k=12.

R1.justification: Related work is refocused from character-information probing toward prior SAE precision/recall limitations, adding Kissane, Templeton and Olah’s July update and explaining how this study extends them. Structured-sparsity and BatchTopK references are added, while the Kaushal–Mahowald and Watkins–Bloom character-information discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and discussion are substantially rewritten around hierarchical absorption. V5 adds a glossary and extensive explanatory appendix sections, standardizes feature/latent terminology, and moves the ablation algorithm from the main text to Appendix A.4. This materially changes the narrative and organization.

P2.justification: V5 replaces Figure 1’s feature-splitting diagram with an encoder/decoder comparison, adds toy-model heatmaps and activation tables, expands the absorption figure with a third panel, and adds Figure 21’s metric comparison. Typography, table styling and figure placement are revised throughout; most original result graphics are retained and resized.

improvement.justification: V1 leaves the mechanism conjectural and explicitly limits evidence to Gemma/JumpReLU. V5 substantially addresses both weaknesses through controlled experiments, a conditional proof, partial-absorption analyses and additional model/architecture evaluations. The metric-choice experiment also strengthens confidence in the retained qualitative trend. The proof’s restricted scope, small additional SAE sample, omitted code link and inconsistent BatchTopK settings limit the gains, but the stronger mechanistic evidence and broader empirical support establish a substantial overall improvement.
